summary: This program keeps a travel packing list in a List of Strings, prints it as a numbered list, then adds one item and removes another before printing the list again to confirm the changes.

lines.text: A List happily holds the same value more than once, which is exactly what a packing list needs when you are bringing several pairs of socks for a multi-day trip.
List positions start at 0, so the loop counter is printed as i + 1 to give the human-friendly numbering people expect on a checklist, while items.get(i) still uses the real index.
The \n inside the text is an escape sequence that produces a blank line, separating the first printed list from the messages that follow.
Removing by name deletes only the first matching item, so the second "Socks" stays in the list; this is the behavior to expect whenever duplicates are present.
Because the loop asks the list for its own size each time rather than hard-coding 4, printing the list again after adding and removing items needs no changes at all.
